10.1186/s12951-026-04996-w.abstract: The coexistence of breast cancer (BC) and atherosclerosis (AS) is increasingly recognized as an inflammation-driven comorbidity. This study identifies the CXCL2–CXCR2 signaling axis as a pivotal mechanistic link underlying both diseases and introduces a macrophage-mimetic nanoplatform for its targeted inhibition. Differential gene expression and PPI network analyses of GEO datasets revealed CXCL2 as a shared hub gene in BC and AS. Clinical sample analyses further showed that female BC patients with vulnerable carotid plaques or high tumor CXCL2 expression had significantly shorter overall survival and disease-free survival, and multivariate regression confirmed vulnerable carotid plaques as an independent risk factor for poor BC prognosis. Co-expression with CXCR2 was validated in murine comorbidity models, where axis activation enhanced proliferation of BC cells, migration of human carotid artery smooth-muscle cells (HCASMCs), and M2 macrophage polarization through PI3K–AKT–mTOR signaling. To selectively disrupt this pathway, we engineered macrophage membrane-coated liposomal nanovesicles loaded with the CXCR2 antagonist SB225002 (MmLip@SB). The biomimetic coating endowed inflammation-site targeting and immune-evasive properties, enabling efficient delivery to tumor and plaque regions. MmLip@SB treatment markedly reduced tumor growth, plaque burden, and inflammatory cytokine expression while improving tissue architecture. These results establish CXCL2–CXCR2 as a shared inflammatory driver of BC and AS and highlight macrophage-mimetic nanovesicles as a promising dual-acting therapeutic approach.

10.1177/19418744261491840.title: Secondary CNS Lymphoma Masquerading as Recurrent Basal Ganglia Stroke
10.1177/19418744261491840.abstract: The basal ganglia comprise a metabolically active group of nuclei implicated in refining movement and emotion. We present the case of a 52-year-old man with common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) who presented to the hospital with severe thrombocytopenia and concern for recurrent basal ganglia stroke. Three months prior, the patient presented for acute confusion and mydriasis and underwent MRI brain, revealing restricted diffusion in the right basal ganglia. Two months prior, he experienced difficulty speaking, and repeat MRI brain revealed new left basal ganglia diffusion restriction. During this admission, MRI brain was obtained again after presentation for urinary incontinence, hypophonia, and flat affect, showing bilateral basal ganglia diffusion restriction. He subsequently underwent closure of his patent foramen ovale (PFO) and had a repeat MRI brain demonstrating new enhancing lesions in the right external capsule and left lentiform nucleus. Lymph node biopsy confirmed a diagnosis of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) and his basal ganglia lesions were diagnosed as secondary CNS lymphoma that was responsive to chemotherapy. In retrospect, several salient features of the presentation could have raised suspicion for an etiology other than stroke, notably the recurrence of subcortical lesions, dearth of evidence suggesting hypercoagulability of malignancy, and increased risk of lymphoma in the setting of the patient’s longstanding history of CVID. Making the diagnosis of lymphoma more promptly would have enabled sooner treatment and prevented unnecessary procedures and exposure to long-term anticoagulation.

10.3897/afrinvertebr.67.194158.title: Fatumocoris flattirei, a new genus and species of Cotyledon-associated plant bugs from South Africa (Hemiptera, Miridae, Bryocorinae)
10.3897/afrinvertebr.67.194158.abstract: The Cape Floristic Region (CFR) is the most plant-dense Mediterranean-type ecosystem on Earth, but the number of described plant bugs (Heteroptera, Miridae) is relatively small. While Miridae are often host-plant specific, an association with succulent plants is only found in ~20 plant bug species worldwide. A combination of recent fieldwork in South Africa’s Western Cape region and iNaturalist [http://www.inaturalist.org/] observations allows us to document and describe a new genus and species of dicyphine Bryocorinae, Fatumocoris flattirei gen. et sp. nov ., associated with Cotyledon orbiculata L. (Crassulaceae). This new plant bug genus is unusual among dicyphines as it possesses prominent spines on the pronotum, a wider posterior margin of the pronotum, and distinctive dark, white, and reddish coloration. The placement is confirmed with morphological examination and inclusion of Sanger sequence data in a recently published molecular dataset of Miridae. Light microphotographs, SEM micrographs, and female and male genitalic images are provided.

10.6084/m9.figshare.34004598.title: When Cleverness Becomes Its Own Undoing: Ọgbọn Àgbọnjù, Excess and the Ethics of Wisdom in Yorùbá Thought
10.6084/m9.figshare.34004598.abstract: This essay examines the Yorùbá proverb “Ọgbọ́n àgbọ́n jù, a máa pa ọlọ́gbọ́n lára,” understood in the author's family transmission as warning that excessive cleverness can ultimately harm the person who considers himself or herself wise. The reflection emerged from an interactive scholarly session at the Institute of African Studies, University of Ibadan, and was subsequently developed through an intergenerational conversation with the author's 91-year-old father, Samuel Ayọ̀ọlá, who responded to the proverb with a Yorùbá narrative concerning a contested kingship, a disguised masquerader, and the limits of strategic manipulation. Rather than treating the narrative as independently verified historical evidence, the essay approaches it as an orally transmitted interpretive tradition. It situates this material within documented Yorùbá proverbial thought, particularly the cluster of proverbs concerning ọgbọ́n Àgbọ́njù, excessive cleverness or cunning, and related reflections on wisdom, moderation, patience, and learning from others. The essay argues that Yorùbá thought does not reject cleverness; rather, it distinguishes productive wisdom from cleverness that becomes excessive, self-regarding, deceptive, or detached from communal judgement. The discussion further considers the relationship between intelligence and humility, strategy and excess, sacred authority and performance, and individual cleverness and collective knowledge. Haruna Ishola's aláṣejù repertoire is brought into conversation with the proverb as a later popular-cultural articulation of the moral problem of excess, while the precise wording of the cited song passage is treated as family-transmitted rather than independently verified. The essay proposes ọgbọ́n àgbọ́njù as a useful indigenous conceptual category for analysing the paradox whereby an attribute that ordinarily produces success, cleverness, can become destructive when it loses its regulating virtues of humility, restraint, and responsiveness to other people's knowledge.

10.1002/smll.75929.title: M2 Macrophage‐Mimetic Metal‐Organic Framework Nanozyme With Visible‐Light‐Driven Hydrogen Evolution for Uveitis Therapy
10.1002/smll.75929.abstract: ABSTRACT Uveitis poses a severe threat to vision and represents a critical clinical challenge. Conventional therapeutic approaches often exhibit limited efficacy in controlling disease progression and lack efficient mechanisms for managing localized oxidative stress. Given that molecular hydrogen (H 2 ) holds substantial promise for treating oxidative and inflammatory diseases via its selective antioxidant properties, we report a metal–organic framework (MOF) nanozyme‐based hydrogen nanogenerator. This system integrates photocatalytic visible‐light‐triggered H 2 generation with multi‐enzyme‐like antioxidant functions for targeted uveitis management. The engineered Pt‐embedded MOF nanozymes (Pt@MOF) concurrently catalyze hydrogen evolution under visible light and display superoxide dismutase‐ and catalase‐like activities, achieving comprehensive scavenging of overproduced reactive oxygen species (ROS). Furthermore, camouflaging the nanozyme with M2 macrophage‐derived cell membrane vesicles (CMVs) endows the nanoplatform with active inflammation‐targeting ability, thereby enhancing the accumulation in inflamed ocular tissues. Following topical administration, this biomimetic nanomedicine successfully mitigates oxidative stress and suppresses pro‐inflammatory cytokines both in vitro and in a rat model of acute uveitis. Overall, this study underscores the immense potential of integrating light‐driven hydrogen therapy with nanozyme therapy, offering a highly effective strategy that could revolutionize future therapeutic interventions for inflammatory eye diseases.

10.5281/zenodo.22981426.title: Comparative History of the Autonomy of Form
10.5281/zenodo.22981426.abstract: This paper does not ask who first “invented” pictorial abstraction—a question that presupposes a single, implicitly Eurocentric origin. It asks instead how many independent visual traditions rendered form autonomous from its depicted subject, and through which internal logics. Grounded in a comparative dataset of fifty works drawn from eight cultural areas (China, Japan, India, Sub-Saharan Africa, Europe, Oceania, the pre-colonial Americas, the Islamic world), dated from the second millennium BCE to the twentieth century, the analysis records for each work the dominant visual phenomenon, the relation to the visible (mimetic, transformed, non-mimetic), the type of relation to its own tradition (internal, documented transmission, open hypothesis), and the primary museum source. The autonomy of form emerges as a recurrent and structurally plural phenomenon articulated through four distinct logics: calligraphic gesture and active emptiness (China, Japan); ritual and cosmological geometry (India, Africa, Oceania, the Americas); atmospheric and perceptual dissolution (Europe); and doctrinal aniconism (Islamic world). The paper offers neither a linear genealogy nor a claim of priority, but a shared methodological framework and an explicitly incomplete, improvable corpus for future comparative research.

10.5281/zenodo.22974372.title: Indigenous Communication Practices and Their Role in Conflict Resolution and Peacebuilding in Mararaba Udege, Nasarawa State
10.5281/zenodo.22974372.abstract: Background: The persistence of communal conflicts in Nigeria has renewed research interest in indigenous communication practices as locally grounded resources for sustainable peace, yet the specific practices used in communities like Mararaba Udege, Nasarawa State, receive less attention from researchers. Objective: This study examines the indigenous communication practices used for conflict resolution and peacebuilding in Mararaba Udege, Nasarawa L.G.A., Nasarawa State. Method: Anchored in a qualitative case study design, the study examined communicative practices such as oral traditions, proverbs, storytelling, communal dialogues, and the mediatory roles of traditional leaders and elders. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, focus group discussions, and non-participant observation involving community leaders, women, youth, and other key informants and were analysed using thematic analysis, guided by the Indigenous Communication System Theory (ICST). Result: Masquerades and festivals serve as public enforcement and promote peace communication channels; fines and compensation function as restorative rather than punitive justice; and the council of elders and traditional leadership structures serve as central judicial bodies for conflict resolution. Conclusion: These indigenous communication practices build trust, legitimacy, and local ways of conflict resolution, contributing to violence prevention and peace consolidation in Mararaba Udege, Nasarawa State. Unique Contribution: The study provides empirically grounded documentation of indigenous communication practices in a community affected by conflicts and under-researched, extending ICST to explain how communication legitimacy is locally constructed and sustained. Key Recommendation: Documenting and integrating indigenous communication practices into formal peacebuilding strategies can strengthen local approaches to conflict management in Nigeria, requiring closer collaboration between state institutions, peace practitioners, and local custodians of these practices.

10.1111/trf.70411.title: A functionally distinct HPA ‐1a‐specific alloantibody associated with fetal/neonatal alloimmune thrombocytopenia that activates platelets via FcγRIIa
10.1111/trf.70411.abstract: Abstract Background Fetal/neonatal alloimmune thrombocytopenia (FNAIT) is caused by maternal alloantibodies directed against fetal platelet antigens, most commonly human platelet antigen‐1a (HPA‐1a). These antibodies mediate platelet destruction and can lead to fetal and neonatal thrombocytopenia severe enough to cause life‐threatening organ bleeds. Antibody titer and isotype do not reliably predict disease severity, suggesting additional heterogeneity among anti‐HPA‐1a antibodies. Study Design and Methods We evaluated the effects of five previously characterized HPA‐1a‐specific monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) on platelet activation, platelet aggregation, and induction of intracellular signaling. The involvement of FcγRIIa was examined using FcγRIIa‐blocking antibody IV.3, protein tyrosine kinase inhibitors, and selected monoclonal antibody Fab fragments. Results At saturating concentrations, all five mAbs inhibited thrombin‐induced aggregation. At sub‐saturating concentrations, however, mAb M‐204 uniquely induced spontaneous aggregation and α‐granule secretion in HPA‐1a‐positive human, but not mouse, platelets, which lack FcγRIIa. M‐204‐induced aggregation was abolished by mAb IV.3 and inhibitors of Src‐ and Syk‐family kinases and was absent using M‐204 Fab fragments. M‐204 induced tyrosine phosphorylation of Syk and PLCγ2 in an FcγRIIa‐dependent manner. Finally, despite persistent platelet activation induced by M‐204, saturating concentrations of this antibody blocked the binding of the fibrinogen mimetic antibody, PAC‐1, to HPA‐1a homozygous, but not HPA‐1a/1b heterozygous, platelets, consistent with the known ability of HPA‐1a‐specific antibodies to sterically interfere with ligand binding to HPA‐1a‐positive αIIbβ3. Conclusion These findings identify a previously unrecognized, functionally distinct subset of HPA‐1a antibodies capable of activating platelets via FcγRIIa, suggesting a potential mechanism contributing to variability in disease severity in FNAIT.

10.1021/acssensors.6c02671.title: Fingerprint-Mimetic Fibrous Glove via Shear-Induced Alignment and Dynamic Compensation for Multimodal Tactile Sensing
10.1021/acssensors.6c02671.abstract: Abstract Flexible devices are key for human–machine interaction in smart homes and virtual reality. However, existing wearable devices are limited by single-mode sensing, irreversible conductive network damage under deformation, and a lack of tactile enhancement, hindering high sensitivity and multimodal perception. Herein, inspired by the arc-shaped topology of human fingerprints, we propose a fiber-based multimodal tactile smart glove (silver/ionic liquid/TPU glove, named SIT Glove). Using Jeffery orbit dynamics, shear flow during wet-spinning aligned silver nanoflakes (AgNFs) axially, while an ionic liquid served as a dynamic conductive compensation medium, yielding SIT fibers with an “electronic network + ionic polarization” synergy. The fibers exhibit excellent strain, pressure, and temperature sensing properties: conductivity 1.66 × 104 S/m, elongation at break 387.96%, gauge factor 9826.244 (80–100% strain), pressure sensitivity 4.4340 kPa–1 (50–60 kPa), and TCR –0.0453 °C–1 (30–40 °C). Meanwhile, embroidering SIT fibers onto glove fingertips in fingerprint patterns created an 18-channel tactile array. Furthermore, with machine learning for gesture recognition and deep learning (1D-CNN) for fabric classification, the glove achieved 93.98% accuracy for 6 gestures and 86.84% for 4 fabrics and demonstrated body temperature monitoring, hot/cold sensing, virtual game interaction, and fan control. This work offers a bioinspired paradigm for wearable devices with high sensitivity, a wide response range, and multifunctional integration.

10.5281/zenodo.22976740.abstract: ଉତ୍ତର-ଉପନିବେଶବାଦ (Post-colonial) ସମୟଖଣ୍ଡରେ ପ୍ରବାସୀ ମନସ୍ତତ୍ତ୍ୱ, ନିର୍ବାସନ, ବିସ୍ଥାପନ ଓ ଆତ୍ମପରିଚୟର ଅନ୍ୱେଷଣ ସମକାଳୀନ ସାହିତ୍ୟ ତତ୍ତ୍ୱର ମୁଖ୍ୟ ବିଷୟବସ୍ତୁ ଭାବେ ଉଭା ହୋଇଛି।। ଓଡ଼ିଆ କଥାକାର ଶରତ ଚନ୍ଦ୍ର ମିଶ୍ରଙ୍କ ଗଳ୍ପ ସଙ୍କଳନ ‘ଅଭିଳାଷ ଓ ଅନ୍ୟାନ୍ୟ ଗଳ୍ପ’ (୧୯୯୪) ଏହି ଦୃଷ୍ଟିକୋଣରୁ ଏକ ଅତ୍ୟନ୍ତ ଉଲ୍ଲେଖନୀୟ ଦୃଷ୍ଟାନ୍ତ। ଓଡ଼ିଆ କ୍ଷୁଦ୍ରଗଳ୍ପର ଧାରାରେ ଆଞ୍ଚଳିକତା ତଥା ପାରମ୍ପରିକ ଗ୍ରାମୀଣ-ମଧ୍ୟବିତ୍ତ ପରିସରରୁ ଊର୍ଦ୍ଧ୍ୱକୁ ଯାଇ ଏକ ବିଶ୍ୱସ୍ତରୀୟ ପରିପ୍ରେକ୍ଷୀ (Global Perspective) ପ୍ରଦାନ କରିବାରେ ଶରତ ଚନ୍ଦ୍ର ମିଶ୍ରଙ୍କ ଗଳ୍ପଗୁଡ଼ିକ ଅନନ୍ୟ। 'ଅଭିଳାଷ ଓ ଅନ୍ୟାନ୍ୟ ଗଳ୍ପ' ସଙ୍କଳନରେ ଥିବା ବାରଟି ଗଳ୍ପ ମାଧ୍ୟମରେ ଲେଖକ ଆଧୁନିକ ମଣିଷର ଆତ୍ମପରିଚୟ ସନ୍ଧାନ (Identity Crisis), ପ୍ରବାସୀ ଜୀବନର ବିଛିନ୍ନତାବୋଧ (Alienation), ଭୌଗୋଳିକ ସୀମାରେଖା ଅତିକ୍ରମ କରି ମଧ୍ୟ ମାନସିକ ସ୍ତରରେ ରହିଯାଉଥିବା ଅପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣତା ବା ‘ଅନୁପସ୍ଥିତି’ (Sense of Absence) ଏବଂ ପ୍ରଶାସନିକ-ଅମଲାତାନ୍ତ୍ରିକ ଦ୍ୱନ୍ଦ୍ୱକୁ ନିଖୁଣ ଭାବେ ରୂପାୟିତ କରିଛନ୍ତି। ଏହା କ୍ଷୁଦ୍ରଗଳ୍ପର ଭୌଗୋଳିକ ସୀମାକୁ ବିଶ୍ୱ ପରିସର ମଧ୍ୟକୁ ପ୍ରସାରିତ କରିଛି। ଉପନିବେଶବାଦୀ ଶାସନର ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ କାଳରେ ଘଟିଥିବା ଦେଶ ବିଭାଜନ, ରାଜନୈତିକ ଉତ୍ଥାନ-ପତନ ଏବଂ ଅର୍ଥନୈତିକ ସ୍ୱପ୍ନ, ରାଜନୈତିକ ସୀମାରେଖା ଓ ପାଶ୍ଚାତ୍ୟ ଭୌତିକତାବାଦ କିପରି ତୃତୀୟ ବିଶ୍ୱର ମଣିଷକୁ ନିଜ ମାଟିରୁ ବିଚ୍ଛିନ୍ନ କରି ବିଦେଶୀ ଭୂଖଣ୍ଡରେ ଏକ ‘ଅନ୍ୟାନ୍ୟ’ (Other) ବା ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଶ୍ରେଣୀର ନାଗରିକ ଭାବେ ଠିଆ କରିଦିଏ, ତାହା ଏହି ସଙ୍କଳନର ମୂଳ ସ୍ୱର। ହୋମି ଭାଭା (Homi Bhabha)ଙ୍କ ‘ସଙ୍କରତା’ (Hybridity), ‘ଅନୁକରଣ’ (Mimicry) ଏବଂ ଷ୍ଟୁଆର୍ଟ ହଲ୍ (Stuart Hall)ଙ୍କ ‘ସାଂସ୍କୃତିକ ଆତ୍ମପରିଚୟ’ (Cultural Identity) ତତ୍ତ୍ୱକୁ ଆଧାର କରି ଏହି ନିବନ୍ଧରେ ଶରତ ମିଶ୍ରଙ୍କ ପ୍ରମୁଖ ଗଳ୍ପଗୁଡ଼ିକର ଏକ ତାତ୍ତ୍ୱିକ ଅନୁଶୀଳନ କରାଯାଇଛି।

10.1038/s41746-026-03276-z.title: Quantifying the plausibility gap in generative AI for surgical video generation with expert assessment
10.1038/s41746-026-03276-z.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) shows promise for physical simulation, yet its clinical application remains critically unexplored. We present SurgVeo, a pioneering expert-guided benchmark paired with the Surgical Plausibility Pyramid framework. Evaluating the Veo-3 and Wan2.2 models reveals a consistent plausibility gap: despite high visual fidelity, the majority of errors are surgical logic failures rather than visual quality deficits. By exposing this reliance on visual synthesis, this study provides a roadmap for developing surgical world models.

10.5281/zenodo.22976665.abstract: ଉତ୍ତର-ଉପନିବେଶବାଦ (Post-colonial) ସମୟଖଣ୍ଡରେ ପ୍ରବାସୀ ମନସ୍ତତ୍ତ୍ୱ, ନିର୍ବାସନ, ବିସ୍ଥାପନ ଓ ଆତ୍ମପରିଚୟର ଅନ୍ୱେଷଣ ସମକାଳୀନ ସାହିତ୍ୟ ତତ୍ତ୍ୱର ମୁଖ୍ୟ ବିଷୟବସ୍ତୁ ଭାବେ ଉଭା ହୋଇଛି।। ଓଡ଼ିଆ କଥାକାର ଶରତ ଚନ୍ଦ୍ର ମିଶ୍ରଙ୍କ ଗଳ୍ପ ସଙ୍କଳନ ‘ଅଭିଳାଷ ଓ ଅନ୍ୟାନ୍ୟ ଗଳ୍ପ’ (୧୯୯୪) ଏହି ଦୃଷ୍ଟିକୋଣରୁ ଏକ ଅତ୍ୟନ୍ତ ଉଲ୍ଲେଖନୀୟ ଦୃଷ୍ଟାନ୍ତ। ଓଡ଼ିଆ କ୍ଷୁଦ୍ରଗଳ୍ପର ଧାରାରେ ଆଞ୍ଚଳିକତା ତଥା ପାରମ୍ପରିକ ଗ୍ରାମୀଣ-ମଧ୍ୟବିତ୍ତ ପରିସରରୁ ଊର୍ଦ୍ଧ୍ୱକୁ ଯାଇ ଏକ ବିଶ୍ୱସ୍ତରୀୟ ପରିପ୍ରେକ୍ଷୀ (Global Perspective) ପ୍ରଦାନ କରିବାରେ ଶରତ ଚନ୍ଦ୍ର ମିଶ୍ରଙ୍କ ଗଳ୍ପଗୁଡ଼ିକ ଅନନ୍ୟ। 'ଅଭିଳାଷ ଓ ଅନ୍ୟାନ୍ୟ ଗଳ୍ପ' ସଙ୍କଳନରେ ଥିବା ବାରଟି ଗଳ୍ପ ମାଧ୍ୟମରେ ଲେଖକ ଆଧୁନିକ ମଣିଷର ଆତ୍ମପରିଚୟ ସନ୍ଧାନ (Identity Crisis), ପ୍ରବାସୀ ଜୀବନର ବିଛିନ୍ନତାବୋଧ (Alienation), ଭୌଗୋଳିକ ସୀମାରେଖା ଅତିକ୍ରମ କରି ମଧ୍ୟ ମାନସିକ ସ୍ତରରେ ରହିଯାଉଥିବା ଅପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣତା ବା ‘ଅନୁପସ୍ଥିତି’ (Sense of Absence) ଏବଂ ପ୍ରଶାସନିକ-ଅମଲାତାନ୍ତ୍ରିକ ଦ୍ୱନ୍ଦ୍ୱକୁ ନିଖୁଣ ଭାବେ ରୂପାୟିତ କରିଛନ୍ତି। ଏହା କ୍ଷୁଦ୍ରଗଳ୍ପର ଭୌଗୋଳିକ ସୀମାକୁ ବିଶ୍ୱ ପରିସର ମଧ୍ୟକୁ ପ୍ରସାରିତ କରିଛି। ଉପନିବେଶବାଦୀ ଶାସନର ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ କାଳରେ ଘଟିଥିବା ଦେଶ ବିଭାଜନ, ରାଜନୈତିକ ଉତ୍ଥାନ-ପତନ ଏବଂ ଅର୍ଥନୈତିକ ସ୍ୱପ୍ନ, ରାଜନୈତିକ ସୀମାରେଖା ଓ ପାଶ୍ଚାତ୍ୟ ଭୌତିକତାବାଦ କିପରି ତୃତୀୟ ବିଶ୍ୱର ମଣିଷକୁ ନିଜ ମାଟିରୁ ବିଚ୍ଛିନ୍ନ କରି ବିଦେଶୀ ଭୂଖଣ୍ଡରେ ଏକ ‘ଅନ୍ୟାନ୍ୟ’ (Other) ବା ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଶ୍ରେଣୀର ନାଗରିକ ଭାବେ ଠିଆ କରିଦିଏ, ତାହା ଏହି ସଙ୍କଳନର ମୂଳ ସ୍ୱର। ହୋମି ଭାଭା (Homi Bhabha)ଙ୍କ ‘ସଙ୍କରତା’ (Hybridity), ‘ଅନୁକରଣ’ (Mimicry) ଏବଂ ଷ୍ଟୁଆର୍ଟ ହଲ୍ (Stuart Hall)ଙ୍କ ‘ସାଂସ୍କୃତିକ ଆତ୍ମପରିଚୟ’ (Cultural Identity) ତତ୍ତ୍ୱକୁ ଆଧାର କରି ଏହି ନିବନ୍ଧରେ ଶରତ ମିଶ୍ରଙ୍କ ପ୍ରମୁଖ ଗଳ୍ପଗୁଡ଼ିକର ଏକ ତାତ୍ତ୍ୱିକ ଅନୁଶୀଳନ କରାଯାଇଛି।

10.1186/s41181-026-00506-3.title: In vivo tracking of nanoerythrosomes with gallium-68 labeling strategies
10.1186/s41181-026-00506-3.abstract: Abstract Background Nanoerythrosomes (NanoEs) are extracellular vesicle mimetics that are suitable for large-scale manufacturing utilizing donated human blood. NanoEs can be used as drug carriers for both disease treatment and diagnostics. To understand the whole-body in vivo behavior of NanoEs, we used positron emission tomography (PET) imaging to study their biodistribution. In this study, we used the [ 68 Ga]Ga- tris (8-hydroxyquinoline) complex to radiolabel NanoEs and track their biodistribution in vivo in healthy Sprague-Dawley rats. The biodistribution was compared with that of the rat control groups administered with [ 68 Ga]GaCl 3 , [ 68 Ga]Ga- tris (8-hydroxyquinoline), and [ 68 Ga]GaCl 3 -labeled NanoEs. Results [ 68 Ga]Ga- tris (8-hydroxyquinoline)-NanoE was synthesized in a two-step process, with a synthesis time of 77 ± 9 min ( n = 4) and a decay-corrected radiochemical yield of 35 ± 20% ( n = 4). The product was purified using size exclusion chromatography and analyzed using thin layer chromatography. The radiotracer was administered to the rats, followed by 60-min PET imaging, after which the tissues were collected for radioactivity quantification. [ 68 Ga]Ga- tris (8-hydroxyquinoline)-NanoE had significantly higher uptake in the liver, pancreas, and blood cells than the control groups. Conclusions It is feasible to radiolabel NanoEs as a novel type of biocompatible nanomaterial with [ 68 Ga]Ga- tris (8-hydroxyquinoline), and significant differences in PET imaging and biodistribution were observed in several tissues compared with the control groups. This is a step forward in the development of NanoE-based delivery platforms for PET imaging and therapeutic purposes.

10.1038/s44321-026-00528-z.title: The therapeutic potential of transposable element activity modulation
10.1038/s44321-026-00528-z.abstract: Abstract The reactivation of transposable elements (TEs) is a recurrent molecular event across cancer, neurodegeneration, autoimmune disease, and aging, yet its therapeutic implications remain largely unexplored. Normally repressed under strict epigenetic surveillance, reactivated transposable elements can generate immunostimulatory nucleic acids that engage cytosolic pattern-recognition receptors, converging on type I interferon signaling and driving chronic sterile inflammation. Yet this inflammatory potential is inherently dual: the same reactivation that drives pathology in some contexts can be harnessed to prime immunity in others. Here, we review two complementary strategies that exploit this duality. Suppressive approaches, including nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors, antisense oligonucleotides, and epigenetic silencing agents, aim to quench pathological TE-driven inflammation in diseases and restore other adaptive mechanisms governing homeostasis. Conversely, controlled TE reactivation through epigenetic priming can induce a viral mimicry state in tumor cells, sensitizing them to immune checkpoint blockade. In parallel, TE-derived peptides presented on MHC class I molecules are emerging as a largely unexploited reservoir of shared tumor antigens for next-generation vaccines and engineered T cell therapies. Together, these observations reframe transposable elements not as mere viral relics to be tolerated, but as a tunable immunological switch whose therapeutic modulation holds promise across some of the most challenging diseases of our time.

10.5281/zenodo.23124264.title: Modular Biomimetics: Programming Macroscopic Phase and Catalytic Function in Non-Protein Artificial Enzymes via Central Metal Substitution. Part IV: Programmable Topological Switches in Organometallic Enzyme Mimetics: Resolving Apoptotic Activation via ΔpK_a Triggers.
10.5281/zenodo.23124264.abstract: Classical chemotherapeutic agents and conventional prodrugs rely on structural degradation or indiscriminate reactivity to achieve cytotoxicity, inherently leading to severe systemic side effects. This paper presents an orthogonal paradigm based on topological Phase Dynamics, introducing a triad of organometallic enzyme mimetics (Pt, Cd, and Fe masked by nicotinamide/pidolic acid ligands). Unlike classical pharmacological agents, these complexes operate as topologically closed quantum switches. They do not undergo physical molecular fragmentation to reach the active state; rather, they are activated by a highly localized -driven deprotonation trigger within the acidic tumor microenvironment. Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules (QTAIM) calculations demonstrate a profound topological dichotomy: classical Cisplatin exhibits an intrinsically chaotic electronic structure characterized by 0 non-nuclear attractor critical points (NNACPs), leaving its heavy metal center completely unshielded and susceptible to erratic, multi-axial electronic fragmentation. Conversely, the designed Fe-NAM complex generates a strictly disciplined, programmable thermodynamic reservoir defined by an octal symmetric configuration of 8 NNACPs. It must be explicitly noted that empirical evaluations of in vivo pharmacokinetics (PK), pharmacodynamics (PD), and targeted testing on biological cell lines fall strictly outside the scope of this theoretical and structural study.

10.1016/j.reth.2026.101181.title: Multifunctional hydrogel scaffolds for endogenous osteochondral regeneration
10.1016/j.reth.2026.101181.abstract: Osteochondral defects, frequently resulting from trauma, infection, or degenerative joint disease, present a significant clinical challenge due to their limited intrinsic healing capacity. Conventional cell-based therapies face limitations including immune rejection, high costs, and regulatory hurdles. Endogenous tissue engineering, which harnesses the body's own repair machinery through biomaterial-mediated recruitment and differentiation of host stem cells, offers a promising alternative. Hydrogel scaffolds, owing to their extracellular matrix-mimetic architecture, tunable physicochemical properties, and capacity for bioactive factor delivery, have emerged as versatile platforms for endogenous osteochondral regeneration. This review provides a strategic overview of hydrogel-based endogenous tissue engineering, covering: (1) the biological rationale for leveraging host cell sources; (2) the design of hydrogels as extracellular matrix -mimetic niches; (3) key regulatory factors; (4) innovative material design strategies. We also discuss current challenges related to long-term functionality, scaffold integration, and clinical translation, offering insights into the development of next-generation hydrogel systems for minimally invasive and effective osteochondral regeneration.

10.1021/acs.analchem.6c04801.title: Cell-Mimetic Compartmentalization of Natural Enzymes within MOF-Core/COF-Shell Heterostructures as a Versatile Cascade Biosensing Platform
10.1021/acs.analchem.6c04801.abstract: Abstract The burgeoning demand for efficient multienzyme cascades necessitates advanced scaffolds capable of precise spatial organization; however, constructing heterostructured multilayer frameworks (HMFs) remains a formidable challenge due to harsh solvothermal conditions and imprecise enzyme localization. Herein, a biocompatible, interface-directed strategy is reported to engineer a cell-mimetic metal–organic framework@covalent organic framework (MOF@COF) heterostructure as a versatile colorimetric biosensing platform. Specifically, glucose oxidase immobilization within defect-rich (COOH)2-UiO-66 via competitive coordination generated robust sensing elements. Subsequently, ionic liquid-catalyzed interfacial nucleation orchestrated the in situ growth of a horseradish peroxidase-encapsulated COF shell, yielding a compartmentalized architecture with hierarchical channels. Mechanistic investigations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the support’s defect density and interfacial adsorption energy, rather than long-range crystallinity, dictate the directional assembly of the COF layer. This heterostructure exhibits enhanced cascade activity and analytical reliability through spatial proximity and reduced mass transfer resistance over conventional one-pot or stepwise assemblies, while control studies with zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 and hydrogen-bonded organic framework counterparts underscore its superiority in proximity-induced intermediate transfer. Integrating monomer reactivity with topological symmetry offers a predictive blueprint for customizing structurally diverse HMF libraries. Ultimately, flexible replacement of the core enzyme enables the functional validation of this platform through the colorimetric quantification of glucose and hypoxanthine, offering a rational blueprint for engineering biointerfaced heterostructures in cascade biocatalysis.

10.3389/fphar.2026.1931941.title: In vitro pharmacological profiling of ITE amide bioisosteric aryl hydrocarbon receptor agonist
10.3389/fphar.2026.1931941.abstract: Previously, we reported ITE-derived bioisostere 2-(1 H -indole-3-carbonyl)-N-methyl thiazole-4-carboxamide (ITE-CONHCH 3 ) as a high-affinity ligand and potent agonist of the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) with anti-colitis properties. In the current study, we present its initial in vitro pharmacological profiling. Physicochemical analysis revealed low aqueous solubility (22 µM), excellent chemical stability in human and mouse plasma, and strong plasma protein binding (>98%). Off-target screening against steroid and nuclear receptors confirmed high AhR selectivity. In Caco-2 cells, ITE-CONHCH 3 exhibited high permeability with no active efflux. Interestingly, the compound partitioned substantially into mouse red blood cells (47%) but only weakly into human RBCs (16%). In reporter gene assays, ITE-CONHCH 3 displayed ∼40-fold higher agonist potency in human cells compared to mouse cells. Its ability to activate AhR was further validated by a cell-free AhR-ARNT heterodimerization assay and by the induction of canonical ( CYP1A1 ) and non-canonical ( PAI-1 ) genes expression in Caco-2 cells. In conclusion, ITE-CONHCH 3 possesses a favorable pharmacological profile supporting its potential preclinical development. However, the observed differences in RBC partitioning and AhR potency between species must be considered when interpreting mouse-derived data.

10.37275/oaijmr.v6i5.946.title: Pre-Lacrimal Medial Canthal Epidermoid Cyst Mimicking Lacrimal Sac Dacryocystocele: An Observational Analytic Investigation of Clinico-Radiological Discordance, Functional Patency, and En Bloc Microdissection
10.37275/oaijmr.v6i5.946.abstract: Background: Subcutaneous medial canthal masses present a diagnostic challenge due to their proximity to the lacrimal drainage system. Epidermoid cysts in this location are rare and frequently masquerade as dacryocystoceles or lacrimal sac tumors, risking inadvertent lacrimal instrumentation. Objective: To characterize a medial canthal epidermoid cyst mimicking dacryocystocele and assess how functional lacrimal testing and imaging guide diagnosis and excision. Methods: An observational-analytic single-case investigation was conducted in a 21-year-old female presenting with a painless left medial canthal mass. A diagnostic protocol integrating quantitative caliper measurements, Anel irrigation syringing, orbital contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT), and en bloc transcutaneous microdissection was implemented with serial trajectory monitoring over 12 weeks. Result: Physical examination revealed a 15 × 10 mm firm, mobile, non-tender subcutaneous mass superficial to the anterior lacrimal crest. Preoperative Anel syringing demonstrated 100% unobstructed patency into the nasopharynx without punctal reflux, excluding intrinsic lacrimal sac stenosis. Contrast CT revealed a 15 × 10 mm homogeneous pre-lacrimal cystic lesion (22.4 ± 4.2 Hounsfield units) with intact adjacent bone and an incidental middle cranial fossa Galassi type II arachnoid cyst. Complete en bloc surgical excision was achieved via an 8-mm skin crease incision preserving capsular integrity and the medial palpebral ligament. Histopathology confirmed an epidermoid cyst lined by mature stratified squamous epithelium containing lamellated orthokeratin without adnexa. Postoperative follow-up demonstrated complete mass resolution (Δ% = -100%), patent lacrimal outflow, and excellent cosmetic healing. Conclusion: Functional lacrimal irrigation and high-resolution computed tomography resolve clinico-radiological discordance between pre-lacrimal epidermoid cysts and true dacryocystoceles. En bloc microdissection with capsular preservation yields definitive cure without lacrimal morbidity.

10.3389/fimmu.2026.1827486.title: Human macrophages activate a coordinated program linking inflammation and cell death in response to intracellular Poly(I:C)
10.3389/fimmu.2026.1827486.abstract: Background Macrophages sense viral double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) via the innate immune receptors TLR3 and MDA5 whose activation drives a robust inflammatory program, often coupled to cell death. TLR3/TRIF-dependent apoptosis has been described in response to dsRNA. Growing evidence suggests that dsRNA may trigger multiple forms of cell death with mechanisms yet to be elucidated. In addition to TLR/TRIF axis, the necroptosis regulator RIPK3 has been implicated in both inflammatory response and cell death during viral infections in several cell types. However, its role in regulating these two events in human macrophages remains unclear. Methods Here, we investigated in human monocyte-derived macrophages (hMDMs) the mechanisms of dsRNA induced cell death and its temporal and molecular linkage to inflammatory signaling, with a focus on the interplay between RIPK3 and the TLR3/TRIF pathways. Results We found that intracellular Poly(I:C), a synthetic analogue of dsRNA, induced cell death with apoptotic and necroptotic features. TRIF-mediated signaling cascade and RIPK3 jointly contributed to caspase-8 activation leading to apoptosis. RIPK3 also promoted necroptosis by inducing MLKL phosphorylation. Downstream of caspases, Poly(I:C) induced cleavage of Gasdermin E (GSDME), which remained intracellular and localized in mitochondria contributing to the amplification of caspase-3 activation. RIPK3-dependent signaling drove the release of IFN-β and TNF-α and promoted the upregulation of the sensors TLR3 and MDA5, thereby amplifying the inflammatory axis. The inflammatory response preceded cell death, with RIPK3 being the key regulator of the early signaling and TLR3/TRIF becoming involved at later timepoints. Conclusions Collectively, these findings identify RIPK3 as key mediator coordinating dsRNA-induced inflammatory signaling and regulated cell death in human macrophages.

10.3389/fonc.2026.1918612.abstract: Mixed epithelial and stromal tumor of the kidney (MEST) is a rare renal neoplasm with biphasic differentiation comprising epithelial and stromal components. It typically appears as a mixed cystic-solid mass on imaging, and the prognosis is favorable in the vast majority of cases. We report a case of MEST with a prominent fat component on imaging: a 54-year-old woman was admitted with a 1-month history of left flank distension and pain. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) showed a mixed cystic-solid mass at the lower pole of the left kidney, with a prominent low-attenuation fat-density area surrounding the mass. Preoperatively, the lesion was considered an unusual angiomyolipoma with epithelial cysts (AMLEC). Because the lesion was small, located at the lower pole, and relatively well circumscribed, the patient underwent laparoscopic left partial nephrectomy. Postoperative histopathologic examination confirmed that the left renal mass was benign; however, immunohistochemistry (IHC) demonstrated positivity for EMA and PCK in the epithelial component and for PR and ER in the stromal component, supporting a diagnosis of MEST. The adipose tissue submitted separately with the tumor was located around the tumor and could not be definitively confirmed as an intratumoral component. This case demonstrates that MEST may also exhibit prominent adipose tissue on imaging and illustrates the diagnostic pitfall in which fat-related imaging findings cause MEST to mimic AMLEC, making the early distinction between MEST and cystic change in fat-containing renal tumors challenging.

10.3389/fphar.2026.1924670.title: microRNA-15b modulates stress-induced premature senescence in chronic doxorubicin cardiomyopathy
10.3389/fphar.2026.1924670.abstract: Introduction Doxorubicin (DOX) is the most widely used anthracycline in hematologic and solid tumors, whose clinical utility is constrained by dose-dependent cumulative cardiotoxicity that can progress to chronic heart failure. Although previously attributed to overt cardiomyocyte loss, emerging evidence indicates that stress-induced premature senescence (SIPS) constitutes the dominant mechanism of chronic cardiotoxicity at clinically relevant concentrations. SIPS is defined by permanent cell cycle arrest, activation of the p53/p21 and p16/Rb tumor suppressor axes, mitochondrial dysfunction, and a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) that sustains a pro-inflammatory myocardial milieu. Nevertheless, the post-transcriptional mechanisms that govern this process remain incompletely understood. Methods The post-transcriptional regulation of DOX-induced SIPS was evaluated in vitro using neonatal rat ventricular myocytes (NRVMs) exposed to sublethal DOX (0.1 μM) with or without prophylactic miR-15b restoration via a synthetic mimetic to assess the p53/p21, p16, SASP, lysosomal, and mitochondrial responses. In vivo , a chronic cardiotoxicity model was established in female C57BL/6 mice receiving a cumulative dose of 30 mg/kg DOX to analyze myocardial miR-15b suppression, SIPS markers, and SASP profiles across survival cohorts. Results Sublethal DOX treatment (0.1 μM) suppressed miR-15b expression by approximately 50% in NRVMs, resulting in post-transcriptional derepression of its mitochondrial target, SIRT4. This miR-15b loss triggered a multiparametric SIPS phenotype encompassing accumulation of γH2AX foci, p53/p21 and p16 activation, SASP induction (IL-6, IL-1β, Mcp-1 and Mmp13), lysosomal dysfunction (increased SA-β-Gal staining) and mitochondrial dysfunction. Prophylactic restoration of miR-15b via a synthetic mimetic selectively attenuated the p53/p21 axis, genomic damage foci, lysosomal dysfunction, mitochondrial dysfunction and SASP (IL-6 and IL-1β), without rescuing the p16/Rb pathway. In the female C57BL/6 chronic cardiotoxicity model, the cohort spontaneously stratified into animals completing the protocol (ND; 67%) and a premature death subgroup (PD; 33%). The PD subgroup exhibited the most profound myocardial miR-15b suppression and greater accumulation of SIPS markers, including γH2AX, p16, and reduced Lamin B. Notably, the SASP displayed distinct qualitative profiles between PD and ND animals, suggesting that SASP composition, rather than magnitude alone, determines the cardiotoxic outcome. Conclusion Collectively, these findings position miR-15b as a key post-transcriptional regulator of DOX-induced SIPS in the cardiomyocyte, whose sustained loss associates with cardiotoxicity severity in vivo .

10.3389/fphar.2026.1940174.title: Resolvin D1 attenuates pulmonary hypertension by suppressing pathological connexin 43-mediated gap junctional communication in pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells
10.3389/fphar.2026.1940174.abstract: Background Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is characterized by progressive pulmonary vascular remodeling driven by activation of pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMCs). Resolvin D1 (RvD1), a specialized pro-resolving lipid mediator derived from docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), has vascular protective actions; however, its pharmacological effect on connexin 43 (Cx43)-mediated gap junctional intercellular communication in PH remains unclear. This study investigated whether RvD1 attenuates PH by suppressing pathological formation of gap-junctional Cx43 (GJs-Cx43) in PASMCs. Methods SU5416/hypoxia-induced PH was established in C57BL/6 mice. In vitro , primary mouse PASMCs were cultured under hypoxic conditions to mimic the hypoxic pathological microenvironment and PASMCs activation associated with PH. Pulmonary hemodynamics, right ventricular function and hypertrophy, pulmonary arterial remodeling, and Cx43 distribution in isolated small pulmonary arteries were evaluated in vivo . In PASMCs, biochemical fractionation, Western blotting, immunofluorescence, lucifer yellow dye transfer, cell proliferation and migration assays, and inflammatory and oxidative stress assessments were performed. ZP1609 was used to enhance GJs-Cx43 function in vitro and in vivo . Results RvD1 improved pulmonary hemodynamics and right ventricular adaptation in SU5416/hypoxia-exposed mice. RvD1 also reduced pulmonary arterial wall thickening, elastic lamina remodeling, α-SMA accumulation and PCNA-positive proliferating cells. Mechanistically, SU5416/hypoxia increased total Cx43 and shifted Cx43 toward the GJs-Cx43 formation. RvD1 inhibited GJs-Cx43 formation and attenuated IL-1β, IL-6, ROS and MDA accumulation while partially restoring SOD. In primary PASMCs, hypoxia increased GJs-Cx43 expression, enhanced lucifer yellow dye transfer, and promoted proliferation and migration; these changes were suppressed by RvD1. ZP1609 restored GJs-Cx43-mediated intercellular communication and weakened the inhibitory effects of RvD1 on PASMC inflammatory activation, oxidative stress, proliferation and migration. In vivo , ZP1609 similarly blunted the protection conferred by RvD1 against pulmonary vascular remodeling, right ventricular pressure overload and right ventricular hypertrophy. Conclusion Pathological GJs-Cx43 formation promotes the spread of remodeling-associated signals across PASMCs networks. RvD1 limits pulmonary vascular remodeling by suppressing Cx43-dependent gap junctional communication, identifying GJs-Cx43 as a pharmacologically relevant mechanism underlying the vascular protection afforded by this DHA-derived lipid mediator.

10.3389/fimmu.2026.1934439.abstract: Platelet Factor 4 (PF4), a cationic antimicrobial peptide, serves as a ligand for the myeloid-specific phagocytic receptor CR3 (Mac-1, CD11b/CD18). We previously demonstrated that recombinant dimeric PF4 (rPF4) functions as a bacterial opsonin, enhancing phagocytosis of Gram-positive Staphylococcus aureus and facilitating clearance of both antibiotic-susceptible and methicillin-resistant S. aureus in a mouse model of infectious peritonitis. In this study, we examined whether rPF4 is pathogen-agnostic by assessing its effect on phagocytosis of Gram-negative encapsulated Klebsiella pneumoniae , a WHO Bacterial Priority Pathogen. We demonstrate that rPF4 enhances CR3-mediated phagocytosis of both live and heat-inactivated high-virulence K2 and low-virulence K3 strains of K. pneumoniae by various mouse and human macrophage cell lines, as well as primary neutrophils and macrophages. It also increased phagocytosis of carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae . rPF4 did not directly kill bacteria but acted as an opsonin, binding to the negatively charged bacterial capsule and creating recognition sites for CR3 on leukocytes. In a mouse sepsis model, a single dose of rPF4 significantly enhanced bacterial clearance from the lungs, liver, and peritoneum and reduced bacteremia. Histological analyses showed that rPF4 provided substantial protection to lung and liver tissues against K. pneumoniae -induced damage. Consistent with these findings, rPF4 treatment increased the survival rates of infected mice. These results show that rPF4 effectively targets the capsule, a key virulence factor of K. pneumoniae , thereby reducing the bacterium’s ability to evade the host immune response. Overall, the data suggest a common mechanism in which cationic rPF4, by binding to the negatively charged surfaces of both Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria, diminishes their antiphagocytic properties.

10.3389/frbis.2026.1806846.title: Piezometric architecture and the geometry of plasticity: a proposed electromechanical model of the Fibrosis–Plasticity axis
10.3389/frbis.2026.1806846.abstract: Background Models of fibrosis are largely molecular and cell-centred. How whole-organism load geometry constrains long-term tissue fate is comparatively underspecified. The Fibrosis–Plasticity Axis (FPA), a conceptual continuum from reversible remodelling capacity to structural fixation, is proposed here as an organising frame; the physical steps linking load geometry to position on that continuum have not been articulated as a testable chain. Objective To formulate, and render falsifiable, the hypothesis that deformation-generated electrical phenomena in collagen-rich matrix act as a load-geometry-dependent modulator of remodelling, and to define the constructs required to test it. Approach We synthesise evidence from tissue electromechanics, mechanotransduction and connective-tissue physiology, and grade each proposed causal link by evidence level. Proposed framework We introduce, as constructs original to this work: the Geometric Origin of the Body (GOB), the equilibrium configuration around which load-bearing architecture is organised; the Geometric Optimal Pressure Load (GOPeL), the hypothesised load distribution permitting maximal reversibility; and the Geometric Origin Displacement Index (GODI), a proposed—not operationalised, not validated—index of deviation from GOB. The electromechanical proposal is stated as three nested hypotheses. H1, the broad electromechanical hypothesis, holds that deformation of collagen-rich matrix generates local electrical phenomena—electrokinetic, piezoelectric and potentially flexoelectric—which may modulate the behaviour of matrix-producing cells. H2, nested within H1, holds that a solid-state component contributes at physiological hydration and, because it does not require fluid flow for its generation, would be expected to persist when electrokinetic contributions are reduced. H3, nested within H2, holds that this solid-state component is specifically piezoelectric rather than flexoelectric. Each may fail without the one above it failing. We further propose that chronic load asymmetry is distributed through mechanically continuous tissue and generates locally biased electrical signalling at many sites, rather than an electrical field propagating through the organism. Key discriminating criterion If cellular remodelling phenotype is unchanged when electromechanically active and electrically inert matrices are compared under matched mechanical exposure, across the substrate, cell type and loading regimes tested, the electrical contribution proposed here would not be supported within that experimental domain.

10.17507/tpls.1610.05.title: Diasporic Ecologies of Survival: Ecofeminist Approaches in Firoozeh Dumas’ Funny in Farsi and Souvankham Thammavongsa’s How to Pronounce Knife
10.17507/tpls.1610.05.abstract: Ecofeminism emphasizes the commonality between the experiences of oppressed women and a polluted planet. It is also a method of analysing how much each of these writers brings out the hushed voices of diasporic groups and how much they are connected with nature. This study examines the application of ecofeminism in comparing Firoozeh Dumas’ Funny in Farsi and Souvankham Thammavongsa’s How to Pronounce Knife. This research explores how and why each of these texts relates to Gender, Nature, and Cultural Identity. Dumas and Thammavongsa, in each of their autobiographical narratives, breach Patriarchal traditions and are struggling with environments that shape their identities. Dumas’ Funny in Farsi amusingly defies her struggles with adapting to becoming an Iranian in America and is a subtle satire on Cultural Displacement and Nature. Similarly, Thammavongsa’s collection of short stories, How to Pronounce Knife, voices concern for Lao Immigrants and their struggle with survival and resilience, not only within their environment but also within their societal position. This research examines how these two authors incorporate the concepts of ecofeminism within the description of Gender, Cultural Survival, and Ecological Awareness. It uncovers the intertwining of personal and communal histories with the physical and social landscapes in which they live. Through this comparison, the research identifies the role of environmental and gendered experiences in constructing narratives.

10.5281/zenodo.18413682.title: CREATIVE LEADERSHIP AS A COGNITIVE-SOCIAL BUFFER AGAINST RUMINATION AND ORGANIZATIONAL ANOMIE: THE FULL MEDIATION ROLE OF EMOTIONAL INTELLIGENCE AND EMOTIONAL CAPACITY
10.5281/zenodo.18413682.abstract: Purpose – This study aims to investigate the full mediation effect of Creative Leadership (CL) in the relationship between employee Emotional Capacities (Emotional Contagion (EC), Emotional Intelligence (EI), and Emotion Regulation (ER)) and two critical forms of psychological strain: Rumination (R) and organizational Anomie (A). The research addresses the gap in understanding the specific psychological mechanism through which positive leadership prevents both individual cognitive dwelling and systemic organizational malaise. Design/methodology/approach – A quantitative, cross-sectional research design was employed using a structured, self-administered survey. Data were collected from $N=350$ working professionals. Hypotheses were tested using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), with analysis conducted using SPSS and LISREL. Findings – The proposed structural model achieved an outstanding fit (RMSEA = 0.003). Emotional Contagion (beta = 1.42) was confirmed as the strongest positive predictor of perceived Creative Leadership. Crucially, CL acts as a significant negative buffer against both Anomie (beta = -0.34) and Rumination (beta = -0.29). The results confirmed that CL fully mediates the relationship between employee emotional capacities and strain outcomes. Research limitations/implications – The study's main limitation is its cross-sectional design, which restricts definitive causal inference. Practically, the findings imply that organizations should integrate emotional resonance into CL training to leverage the strong predictive power of Emotional Contagion. Future work should utilize longitudinal designs or test moderators to confirm the causal sequence and explore contextual variations. Originality/value – This paper provides a novel, empirically-validated framework quantifying CL’s role as a cognitive-social buffer against both individual (R) and organizational (A) strain. It uniquely establishes the paramount role of Emotional Contagion as the primary antecedent for effective Creative Leadership perception, refining leadership theory.

10.20517/mns.2026.07.abstract: Mechanical, structural, and physiological changes in the stomach underlie both short- and long-term gastric pathologies, most of which are influenced by disruptions of acid secretion, mucosal barrier integrity, motility, or immune responses. Species-specific distinctions limit the study of the pathophysiological state of the human stomach in preclinical animal models. Organoid and organ-on-a-chip (OoC) technologies are emerging tools for recapitulating the compositional and functional properties of native gastric tissue, thus revolutionizing research in gastric health and disease as well as drug screening. The review summarizes recent progress in the development of organoids to model gastric development and disease states to investigate their underlying mechanisms and evaluate associated treatments. Furthermore, microfluidic-based OoC models of the human stomach with an epithelial lining that interfaces with adjacent tissues (including the endothelium and stroma) are described for their increased physiologic relevance owing to the presence of fluid flow and peristalsis-like motion. Finally, we discuss the engineering challenges of the present organoid/OoCsystems, including cell sourcing, experimental throughput, and scalable fabrication, followed by highlighting the future opportunities regarding the optimization of in vitro gastric models for studying gastric pathophysiology and developing personalized therapeutic agents.

10.25986/iri.2026.104.2.005.abstract: Статья посвящена изучению горизонтальных связей в поручных записях 1560-х – начала 1570-х гг. из Царского архива, которые рассматриваются как единый комплекс документов, отражающий происходившие изменения во внутриполитической ситуации Русского государства. Проделанный анализ позволяет сделать вывод, что поручные записи имели ситуативный характер и не привели к возникновению практики общей поруки среди представителей круга высшей аристократии, по аналогии с территориальными служилыми корпорациями второй половины 1570-х гг. Выявленные примеры горизонтальных связей не отличались системностью. При увеличении сумм поруки и расширении числа поручителей процедура поручительства теряла свое значение и превращалась в своеобразный политический «маскарад». This article examines horizontal connections in the 1560s and early 1570s guarantee notes from the Tsar’s archive, examining them as a unified set of documents reflecting ongoing changes in the domestic political situation of the Russian State. The analysis suggests that the guarantee notes were of situational nature and did not lead to the emergence of a practice of general surety among the upper aristocracy members, similar to the territorial service corporations of the second half of the 1570s. The identified examples of horizontal connections were not systematic. As the sums of surety increased and the number of sureties expanded, the surety procedure lost its significance and turned into a kind of political “masquerade.”

10.1021/acsami.6c10551.abstract: Abstract Graphene–cellulose aerogels offer lightweight and multifunctional platforms, yet their limited mechanical robustness restricts practical deployment. Herein, we report a bioinspired strategy that integrates novel spray-freezing fabrication with a cuttlebone-mimetic wall–septa architecture to achieve multiscale mechanical reinforcement in graphene–cellulose aerogels. The spray-freezing method allows for scalable production, and the resulting aerogels exhibit an ultralow density of 0.077 g/cm3 while achieving a specific strength of 14.80 kN m/kg and specific modulus of 4.51 kN m/kg at 80% compressive strain, corresponding to 4.95 and 4.96 times those of conventional freeze-dried counterparts. Multiscale simulations reveal that the enhancement arises from two primary mechanisms. At the nanoscale, borax-mediated crosslinking enhances cellulose network integrity, while the bending and load redistribution of graphene nanosheets introduce additional energy dissipation pathways within the lamellar framework. At the mesoscale, horizontal septa in the structure effectively relieve stress concentration during high strain compression. The synergistic coupling of molecular reinforcement and architectural stress redistribution establishes a structure-property paradigm for mechanically resilient cellular nanocomposites. This work provides mechanistic insights into bioinspired multiscale reinforcement and offers a scalable platform for engineering high-performance, lightweight graphene-based aerogels, which is expected to be applied in the thermal and fire prevention fields.

10.15294/rainbow.v15i3.63704.title: The Unhomeliness Dilemma of Cultural Identity on Sherman Alexie’s Short Story War Dances
10.15294/rainbow.v15i3.63704.abstract: Sherman Alexie’s (2009) War Dances, one of the short stories in the anthology War Dances, portrays the complexities of Native American identity in contemporary American society. The issue lies in how Indigenous subjects negotiate their cultural belonging through the continuing presence of colonial histories and the supremacy of American cultural values. The narrative presents various social phenomena and catastrophes marked by uncertainty, isolation, and displacement. The contour suggests that cultural identity cannot be comprehended as a settled and homogeneous category, but rather as a negotiated process. This study examines the representation of unhomeliness as cultural identity’s dilemma for Native Americans, employing Homi K. Bhabha’s postcolonial theory, particularly the concepts of hybridity, mimicry, ambivalence, and unhomeliness. Bhabha’s concept of hybridity provides a framework of in-between cultural space that leads to the concept of mimicry as the process of adoption and negotiation between social and cultural entities within the realm of assimilation correlated with ambivalence’s potential. These circumstances culminate in unhomeliness considered not merely as physical displacement but also as a psychological and cultural condition in which the subject experiences a disrupted sense of belonging. The study argues that War Dances portrays unhomeliness as a persistent dilemma in Native American cultural identity.

10.26599/frict.2026.9441322.abstract: Abstract Inspired by sophisticated adhesion strategies in nature, physicochemical properties of pollen from three widely distributed fruit species (apple, pear, and kiwifruit) are investigated, and an novel adhesion mechanism for fruit tree pollination is proposed. Through simulation and measurement of natural pollination process, adhesion force between pollen and stigma is quantified, with its constituent components deduced theoretically. Herein, composition and hygroscopic capacity of pollenkitt from three species reveal that while van der Waals forces dominate the adhesion between two biological interfaces, the presence of pollenkitt confers an increased binding strength as relative humidity rises. At the microscale, pollen surfaces are characterized, and biological model between pollen surface microstructure and stigma papillae is investigated to reproduce the natural pollination adhesion system. Following the discovery of strikingly similar ridge structures in two Rosaceae pollen species and dense microprotuberances on kiwifruit pollen, various mechanical models of these microstructures with papillae as well as artificial substrates are established. Furthermore, based on electrostatic properties of pollen, the electrostatically enhanced adhesion effect is explored through theoretical analysis and experimental validation. Collectively, this research elucidates a bioadhesion mechanism underlying fruit tree pollination, providing application potential for research in agricultural science and technology, biomedicine, and ecological environment.

10.25259/jons_12_2026.title: Halo melanoma of the nail unit: A diagnostic and surgical pitfall
10.25259/jons_12_2026.abstract: Nail unit melanoma (NUM) is a rare but aggressive form of melanoma that often masquerades as a benign nail disorder, leading to diagnostic delay. We report a 60-year-old Indian male who presented with a progressive left thumb nail lesion that evolved from longitudinal melanonychia to destructive nail dystrophy with a friable exophytic mass, together with surrounding periungual depigmentation and focal pigmentation. Onychoscopy revealed an irregular pigment network and black-brown globules over a depigmented background. Positron emission tomography-computed tomography demonstrated a fluorodeoxyglucose-avid primary lesion involving the thumb and a metabolically active ipsilateral axillary lymph node. Histopathology of the amputated specimen confirmed malignant melanoma. Microsections from the depigmented periungual skin showed loss of epidermal melanocytes with dermal melanophages and pigment incontinence, along with scattered atypical melanocytes containing fine granular melanin in continuity with the primary tumour, indicating lateral lentiginous tumour spread within the depigmented field. This case underscores the diagnostic challenges of NUM, in which destructive nail changes may obscure early recognition and periungual depigmentation may mask subclinical lateral tumour spread. Onychoscopy and metabolic imaging are valuable adjuncts for diagnosis and staging; whereas histopathology remains the gold standard. Early suspicion and prompt biopsy are crucial for improving outcomes.

10.1002/ange.2705500.abstract: ABSTRACT Current antibacterial therapies often suffer from limited bacterial selectivity, host‐cell toxicity, and inflammation triggered by toxin release during bacterial killing. Here, we report a neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs)‐mimetic, dopamine‐incorporated DNA net, termed D A Net‐DA, enabling targeted bacterial eradication and concurrent toxin neutralization. Inspired by the trap‐kill‐neutralize function of NETs, D A Net‐DA selectively captures and traps bacteria, followed by in situ catalytic formation of polydopamine nanoshells on the trapped bacteria. This process enables efficient photothermal bacterial eradication while minimizing damage to host cells. Meanwhile, the nanoshells act as molecular sponges to sequester and neutralize bacterial toxins, thereby mitigating toxin‐associated inflammation. These integrated functions endow D A Net‐DA with potent therapeutic efficacy in vivo, as demonstrated by markedly reduced bacterial burdens, toxin levels, tissue inflammation in both conventional and burn wound infection models. Moreover, the simultaneous clearance of bacteria and residual toxins alleviates pro‐inflammatory macrophage polarization, thereby accelerating wound tissue regeneration. This work presents a NETs‐mimetic antibacterial strategy that integrates pathogen clearance with toxin neutralization, offering a promising method for treating bacterial infection‐associated diseases.

Conclusion: BP should be considered in persistent DG in the elderly, as timely biopsy and corticosteroid therapy expedite diagnosis and restore oral health.

10.1021/acsbiomaterials.6c00931.abstract: Abstract Understanding how organic matrix architecture regulates biomineralization remains a central challenge in mineralized tissue regeneration. Emerging evidence highlights the importance of coupled phenomena, including nanoconfinement, ionic and pH regulation, and hierarchical structural remodeling, in directing mineral formation. Silk fibroin (SF) is a versatile structural protein widely used in biomaterials due to its tunable mechanics, scalable processing into micro- and nanoscale constructs, controllable biodegradation, and ability to support cell infiltration and tissue integration, including in bone. However, despite its favorable biological properties, SF exhibits limited intrinsic self-mineralization in physiological fluids, restricting its mechanical reinforcement and osteogenic potential. In this study, we engineered SF scaffolds with controlled microstructure and anisotropy and incorporated bioactive inorganic phases, nano-hydroxyapatite (HA) or 45S5 bioactive glass (BG) to promote self-directed mineralization. Scaffolds were evaluated in simulated body fluid under static and dynamic conditions to assess mineral formation and distribution. Isotropic architectures supported more uniform, volumetric mineral integration, whereas anisotropic scaffolds promoted preferential surface mineral deposition. Incorporation of HA or BG significantly enhanced mineralization, leading to the formation of carbonate-substituted hydroxyapatite (CHA). These compositional and structural effects translated into marked improvements in compressive mechanical properties. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that synergistic control over scaffold architecture and bioactive cargo can direct in situ mineralization, enabling the design of silk-based constructs with enhanced mechanical performance and potential for bone regeneration.

10.18231/j.sajhp.19450.1791625886.abstract: Introduction: Sialolithiasis is the formation of calcified deposits within the salivary gland or its ductal system, most commonly affecting the submandibular gland and Wharton's duct (~80–90% of cases). Most sialoliths are oval or round; however, atypically branched or irregularly shaped calculi are exceedingly rare and may closely simulate malignancy, posing a significant diagnostic challenge. Case Report: A 58-year-old male presented with a 2-month history of progressive, painful left submandibular swelling with difficulty swallowing. He had a habit of chronic tobacco chewing and a history of angina on antiplatelet therapy. Examination revealed a single, round-to-oval, nodular and tender swelling with no discharge or temperature rise. Intraorally, multiple missing teeth, root pieces, and generalised severe attrition were noted. Investigations: Ultrasonography revealed a heteroechoic lesion with linear calcification and increased vascularity on colour Doppler, raising suspicion of a neoplastic process. CECT neck demonstrated an enlarged left submandibular gland with heterogenous enhancement, a calculus in the submandibular duct, surrounding fat stranding, and reactive cervical lymphadenopathy — consistent with acute sialadenitis secondary to sialolithiasis. CBCT further characterised the calculus as a highly radio-opaque structure with a striking irregular branched ginger-root morphology and smooth, well-defined periphery within the left submandibular gland space.Conclusion: This case highlights a rare ginger-root–shaped sialolith masquerading as submandibular malignancy. Multimodal imaging was pivotal in establishing an accurate diagnosis. Clinicians must maintain a high index of suspicion for morphologically atypical sialolithiasis to avoid misdiagnosis and unwarranted surgical intervention.

10.1038/s44319-026-00959-2.title: Viral subversion of B-cell tolerance: mechanisms linking infection to autoimmunity
10.1038/s44319-026-00959-2.abstract: Abstract Viral infections are increasingly recognized as triggers of autoimmunity, yet the mechanisms linking viral infection to breakdown of B-cell tolerance remain incompletely understood. B-cell tolerance is maintained through sequential central and peripheral checkpoints that normally eliminate or silence self-reactive clones. Viral infections converge on shared mechanisms, including inflammatory cytokines, innate immune activation, molecular mimicry, and persistent antigen exposure, while also promoting polyreactivity, thereby enhancing the survival, activation, and expansion of autoreactive B cells. In this review, we propose that autoimmune outcomes are determined less by viral identity than by the immunological and anatomical context in which tolerance fails. We integrate mechanistic and clinical evidence across systemic, localized, and neurotropic viral infections to present a unifying framework for virus-induced B-cell tolerance breakdown. This framework identifies conserved principles underlying post-viral autoimmunity and provides a foundation for developing therapeutic strategies to preserve B-cell tolerance.

10.33232/001c.172274.title: Spectroscopic follow-up of compact object binary candidates from Gaia DR3: White dwarfs, neutron stars, black holes, and the parallax zeropoint
10.33232/001c.172274.abstract: Astrometry and radial velocities (RVs) from Gaia DR3 yielded orbits for hundreds of thousands of binary systems, including several samples proposed to contain black holes (BHs), neutron stars (NSs), and white dwarfs (WDs). We present results of a systematic spectroscopic follow-up program targeting these objects. Beginning with a sample of 227 sources, we used a combination of archival data and many-epoch spectroscopic follow-up to characterize more than 200. We obtained 1292 high-quality RVs over a period of four years using the TRES and FEROS spectrographs, achieving a typical precision of 50 m/s and at least 10 RVs for 60 sources. We use these data to test the Gaia orbital solutions and tighten constraints on orbital parameters and component masses. Joint fitting of astrometry and RVs allows us to directly constrain flux ratios, verifying that undetected companions are genuinely dark. We find that ~60% of the astrometric candidates indeed host compact objects, including the two known Gaia BHs, 27 NS candidates, and a dozen massive WDs. We show that tight WD+WD binaries may masquerade as NSs within this sample. The spectroscopic candidates have lower purity: ~50% have spurious solutions, and a majority of the rest are post-mass-transfer binaries or hierarchical triples. Joint astrometry+RV fits of binaries with dark companions yield direct, parallax-independent distance measurements. Using 40 such systems, we measure the Gaia DR3 parallax zeropoint for astrometric orbital solutions. We find Z = − 0.0362 ± 0.0053 mas, consistent with the single-star zeropoint for sources of similar color and magnitude. These results will guide the selection of cleaner candidate samples from Gaia DR4, where a longer observing baseline will enable discovery of many more compact object binaries. RV follow-up will remain important for confirming individual systems, particularly those with extreme parameters.

10.1186/s43556-026-00594-2.title: An inducible co-stimulator ligand (ICOSL)-based peptide therapy for proteinuric kidney diseases targeting αvβ3 integrin
10.1186/s43556-026-00594-2.abstract: Dysregulated αvβ3 integrin activation in podocytes contributes to proteinuric kidney disease by disrupting podocyte architecture and the glomerular filtration barrier. However, no treatments currently exist that therapeutically target this integrin. We previously identified inducible co-stimulator ligand (ICOSL) as an endogenous antagonist of αvβ3 integrin that protects kidney function through its arginine-glycine-aspartic acid (RGD) motif, independent of its canonical role in immunity. Leveraging the therapeutic advantages of small peptides and the renoprotective function of ICOSL, we used a structure-guided approach to design a 19-amino acid human ICOSL-derived peptide (hICOSL-19) containing the RGD motif and evaluated its therapeutic potential for proteinuric kidney disease. hICOSL-19 exhibited high-affinity binding to αvβ3 integrin, similar to full-length ICOSL, and retained its αvβ3-antagonistic activity. PEGylation of hICOSL-19 (PhICOSL-19) extended its circulating half-life while preserving its antagonistic function. In murine models of acute and chronic proteinuric kidney disease, including immune-mediated glomerulonephritis and diabetic nephropathy, PhICOSL-19 treatment significantly reduced proteinuria, limited glomerular injury, and preserved podocyte architecture. In vitro and in vivo safety assessments further showed no detectable podocyte cytotoxicity, T-cell activation, or anti-drug antibody response. These findings suggest that an ICOSL-derived peptide targeting αvβ3 integrin represents a potential therapeutic strategy for proteinuric kidney diseases associated with αvβ3 integrin activation.

10.54878/7sfyzq64.title: Medieval Arabic Dance: Philosophical and Speculative Foundations of the Performing Arts in the Abbasid Era
10.54878/7sfyzq64.abstract: This paper reconstructs, through a textual and philosophical reading of selected Abbasid-era sources, the pre-expressive foundations of medieval Arabic court dance as an integrated performing art rather than a recoverable “catalogue of steps.” Methodologically, it advances an interpretive hypothesis grounded primarily in al-Fārābī's Kitāb al-mūsīqī al-kabīr and al-Masʿūdī's Murūj al-Ḏahab, supplemented by reflections drawn from al-Kindī's musical theory, while delimiting the investigation to the Abbasid period (second half of the 8th to the first half of the 13th century). The author is a performing scholar—dancer, choreographer, and researcher—whose analysis emerges from nearly thirty years of embodied practice in Arab-Islamic and Persian dance forms, and whose dancer-philosopher perspective combines firsthand performance experience with rigorous philological inquiry. The present work is the second volume of a two-part research project: the first volume (Sales 2006, Akkuaria, Roma) introduced the dancer-philosopher perspective and examined al-Kindī's philosophico-musical principles; the current volume (Sales 2025) extends that inquiry to al-Fārābī and al-Masʿūdī and develops the five-nucleus model of pre-expressive requirements. The approach integrates (i) textual-philological analysis of these witnesses, (ii) a controlled comparative-analogical reading oriented toward Persian and Central-Asian stylemes still attested “without solution of continuity,” and (iii) a dancer-philosopher standpoint developed through long practical experience, in which dance remains inseparable from musical philosophy and its ontological horizon. Results are organized into a five-nucleus model of pre-expressive requirements: professionalisation of the artist; the body as sonic/percussive extension; mimetic dance; defined repertoires and technical abilities; and the organic relationship between musical execution and choreutic practice. The paper concludes that, although reliable textual testimonies appear only from the 10th century, their described richness implies a long prior maturation “not born suddenly from nothing,” and that Abbasid court dance should be understood as multi-competent artistry (dance, song, and rhythmic percussion) structurally intertwined with music and classical Arabic poetry.

10.25258/ijddt.16.87s.10.title: STIMULI-RESPONSIVE POLYMERS: DESIGN PRINCIPLES, POLYMER ARCHITECTURES, AND CONTROLLED FUNCTIONAL RESPONSES
10.25258/ijddt.16.87s.10.abstract: Smart polymers undergo reversible physicochemical changes in response to stimuli such as magnetic fields, temperature, pH, light, and external reagents. Advanced polymerization techniques, including reversible addition fragmentation chain transfer (RAFT), atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP), and ring opening polymerization, enable precise control over polymer architecture and functional group placement, allowing the design of tailored responsive materials. These polymers are widely explored in biomedical applications, drug delivery, biosensing, cosmetics, and soft robotics due to their ability to adapt dynamically to environmental conditions. Poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) is a well-known thermoresponsive polymer extensively studied for drug delivery and sensing. Responsive polymers exist in linear, block, graft, and cross-linked forms, with activation depending on interactions between structural motifs and stimuli. Despite promising results, challenges remain, including immunogenicity, batch variability, synthesis complexity, scalability, and limited understanding of in vivo stimulus accessibility. Covalent adaptable and interpenetrating polymer networks enhance mechanical strength, biocompatibility, and stimuli responsiveness.

10.25258/ijddt.16.88s.2.title: From Inflammation to Resolution: Therapeutic Insights into Chronic Disease Management
10.25258/ijddt.16.88s.2.abstract: Inflammation is a fundamental biological process implicated in various physiological and neurological disorders, including cardiovascular diseases, cancer, diabetes, and neurodegenerative conditions. Chronic inflammation is linked to significant health challenges and mortality worldwide, emphasizing the importance of understanding its mechanisms and resolution. This review elucidates inflammatory processes as essential components of the immune response, highlighting pharmacological interventions for promoting timely inflammation resolution. We explore the dual phases of inflammation—acute and chronic—detailing the complex cellular interactions and signaling pathways that govern the inflammatory response to pathogens and tissue injury. In particular, we emphasize specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs), such as lipoxins and resolvins, which play crucial roles in transitioning inflammation from a detrimental to a healing state. Additionally, we discuss innovative therapeutic approaches, including tissue engineering, cellular therapies, and the utilization of SPMs, aimed at enhancing inflammation resolution. The roles of gaseous mediators and peptide/protein mediators in modulating inflammation are also examined. Through this comprehensive analysis, we advocate for the development of pro-resolving treatments to improve outcomes for patients with chronic inflammatory disorders. By understanding the intricate dynamics of inflammation and its resolution, new avenues for targeted therapy emerge, offering promise for mitigating the impacts of chronic inflammatory diseases and enhancing patient quality of life.

10.31612/2616-4868.7.2026.07.title: JAUNDICE FORM OF LEPTOSPIROSIS IN OBSTETRIC PRACTICE: A CLINICAL CASE OF MATERNAL DEATH
10.31612/2616-4868.7.2026.07.abstract: Introduction. The icteric form of leptospirosis in pregnant women is rare but severe, potentially leading to multi-organ failure and a high risk of maternal and fetal death. Clinical manifestations are often nonspecific and may mimic preeclampsia or other pregnancy complications, complicating early diagnosis.Aim. To increase medical professionals’ awareness of the clinical course and pathomorphological findings of icteric leptospirosis in pregnancy to support timely diagnosis and clinical management.Materials and methods. A retrospective analysis was conducted of a maternal death in a 25-week pregnant woman with the icteric form of leptospirosis. The study included anamnesis, clinical manifestations, laboratory findings, and autopsy results, with macro- and histological examination of the liver, kidneys, lungs, and placenta.Results. On admission, the patient had jaundice, hyperthermia (39.2 °C), tachycardia, arterial hypotension, and oliguria. Laboratory tests indicated severe liver and kidney injury (bilirubin 175 µmol/L, ALT 86 U/L, AST 95 U/L, creatinine 149 µmol/L, urea 15.8 mmol/L, thrombocytopenia 74×10⁹/L, leukocytes 15.4×10⁹/L, C-reactive protein 18 mg/L). Despite intensive therapy, multi-organ failure, disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), and septic shock developed, resulting in death. Autopsy confirmed a severe infectious-toxic process: focal hepatic necrosis, dystrophic and necrotic changes in the kidneys, venous congestion and pulmonary edema, and severe infectious-inflammatory damage of the placenta with villous edema, trophoblast necrosis, and extensive hemorrhages.Conclusions. Clinical, laboratory, and morphological findings indicate a severe course of the icteric form of leptospirosis in pregnancy and confirm the link between systemic infection, impaired uteroplacental circulation, and maternal death. Early involvement of an infectious disease specialist and intensive therapy is critically important.
